🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Alan Jones, the Australian driver who won the 1980 Formula 1 world championship with Williams, has died at 80.

Jones died on Thursday, November 5, 2026, after a short illness, just three days after celebrating his 80th birthday. His wife, Amanda Butler-Davis, announced his death in a statement released through Motorsport Australia.

Born Alan Stanley Jones in Melbourne on November 2, 1946, he worked his way into Formula 1 after arriving in Britain with little money, making his debut in 1975. In 1980, driving for Williams, he won five Grands Prix and beat Nelson Piquet to the drivers' title, becoming Williams' first world champion and only the second Australian to win the championship, after Sir Jack Brabham. He remains Australia's last Formula 1 world champion.

Across his Formula 1 career, Jones won 12 Grands Prix and stood on the podium 24 times. He was appointed an MBE for services to motorsport in 1980 and was inducted into the Sport Australia Hall of Fame. After retiring from racing, he became a television commentator and an FIA steward, and remained one of the sport's most outspoken voices.

Williams paid tribute to its first champion, saying he was instrumental in turning the team into a championship-winning force in only its fourth season in Formula 1. He is survived by his wife, Amanda, and his six children, Christian, Amber, Zara, Jack, Camilla and Emma.

Rest in Peace, Alan Jones.

Sources: Australian Associated Press; Motorsport Australia, statement from Amanda Butler-Davis; Williams Racing; Fox Sports Australia.
